study.question: Does lifecycle v2 (the per-step trust-region curvature clamp) remove the graft's germination-stage divergence on the norm and conv_heavy seeds of the under_normalized host, for the derived reason, without changing the graft where v1 is already safe?
study.scope: Covers both seeds that put kappa above c* on this host (norm, conv_heavy), plus a regression cell, and reports host-arm instability (the seed-2142 static divergence class) as its own criterion. It does not measure graft value: that is a later, separately pre-registered graft-capture study.

units.definition: one training seed in one cell; v1 and v2 of that seed share initialization and every minibatch, and within each run the three arms are matched repeated measures
units.population_note: Inference covers training randomness on one fixed data sample (data_seed 20261004) for the three declared host x seed cells.

endpoint.metric: development cross-entropy (nats) over all 5,000 dev examples
endpoint.per_unit_reduction: mean dev CE over the late epochs per arm; None for an arm that diverged

predictions.c1: Expected pass. Under v2, kappa_t <= 0.5 c* at every STE step by construction, and the witness validator rejects any run that breaks the bound. Probability of 0/48 at a true v2 lifecycle-divergence rate of 0.5% / 1% / 2% / 6.25%: 0.786 / 0.617 / 0.379 / 0.045 ((1-p)^48).
predictions.c2: Expected testable and passing. v1 diverged in 12/48 (positive-control-v1) and 6/16 (reproduction) cell-A units; at a 25% rate, P(no v1 positive in cell A alone) = 0.75^24 = 0.001. Cell B's v1 rate is unmeasured. Sensitivity 1.0 is predicted because kappa > c* is the derived mechanism; AUC >= 0.9 is less certain, because amplification ignores how long the over-limit steps last relative to the seed's initial gain.
predictions.c3: Expected pass: shown bitwise on the 7-epoch smoke pair (test_variant_independent_arms_are_bitwise_equal_across_variants) and the GPU probe shows bitwise replay per device; both variants of one seed run on the same GPU.
predictions.c4: Expected pass. conv_light's raw output scale is not known to put kappa above 0.5 c* on the mild host; if the clamp never engages, v2 equals v1 exactly and every difference is zero.
predictions.c5: Not predicted. The static arm diverged once on this host in positive-control-v2 (seed 2142). C5 reports host-arm divergences; it does not decide acceptance.
predictions.would_surprise: Any v2 lifecycle divergence in A or B; a v1 divergence with max kappa below c*; a replay mismatch.

disclosures: Exploratory engineering acceptance test (docs/bounded-lifecycle-v2.md), pre-registered so the criteria cannot move after the data. It is not a confirmatory study of graft value.
The divergence rate on cell A under v1 is already public (positive-control-v1 12/48; reproduction 6/16), and the mechanism was derived from those runs. C2 tests the derivation on fresh seeds.
data_identity was copied from positive-control-v2 manifests (same data_seed, train_size and dev_size).

Pre-germination scheduled divergences are host instability (the scheduled arm is the no-growth host until its seed exists). They are excluded from C1 and C2 and reported in C5. This rule is declared before launch.
C2 uses the strict reading: every germinated v1 divergence, in any stage, must have shown max kappa_live > c* during STE. The by-stage breakdown is reported.
Execution profile: GPU, Academy-exact per SKU (2x RTX 4060 Ti); GPU lineage only. Both variants of a seed run on the same GPU.
The criteria are computed by experiments/lifecycle_validation.py (evaluate_criteria), whose hash is pinned at launch; the PDR states them in prose.
